name: Rikers Island Bridge
facts: Opened on November 22, 1966, the Rikers Island Bridge replaced a costly ferry service, cutting annual operating expenses by $5,000 and saving the city $410 million in construction costs for island facilities.
The bridge’s 52‑foot rise grants vessels beneath a clear span, while 260 concrete piles—each up to 124 feet long—anchor the girder structure across the East River’s Rikers Island Channel.

Co‑named on May 25, 1978, for Supervising Warden Francis R. Buono, the bridge’s construction was overseen by Buono himself, who later became a pivotal figure in the 1990 labor dispute involving guards barricading access.
